title: Early Islamic jurists and non-four Sunni legal circles
method: Curated named authority nodes for an early/non-four-school visual layer; match works only on work-authorship fields, not title mentions or arbitrary shared subjects
caveats: The madhhab term initially referred to opinions and personal circles; later doctrinal schools crystallized gradually, especially in the 4th/10th century.
A jurist with disciples is not automatically the founder of an enduring doctrinal school.
Source metadata author matches do not prove a work expresses the founder's own settled legal doctrine.
The four later institutional schools must not be anachronistically imposed on works before they formed.
A modern Salafi identity is not added as a classical fifth Sunni madhhab.

authority_statuses.individual_jurist: Named early jurist; following or durable school not established by this register
authority_statuses.historical_nonfour_school: Historically attested named non-four-school legal tradition; longevity varies
authority_statuses.founding_eponym: Early eponym of later institutionalized four-school tradition

authorities.name: al-Awzāʿī
authorities.description: Syrian jurist with historically reported followers and school; the nature of early regional/personal affiliations remains debated.

authorities.name: Sufyān al-Thawrī
authorities.description: Kufan authority with an associated personal school; its continuity and exclusivity are disputed in specialist scholarship.

authorities.name: al-Layth b. Saʿd
authorities.description: Egyptian jurist with a following; not a surviving four-school institution.

authorities.name: Ibn Abī Laylā
authorities.description: Early Iraqi jurist and personal-school exemplar; preserved in legal debates rather than an institutional four-school madhhab.

authorities.name: Abū Thawr
authorities.description: Baghdadi jurist with followers and a non-enduring legal circle; not equivalent to a later fully articulated madhhab.

authorities.name: Dāwūd al-Ẓāhirī / Ẓāhirīs
authorities.description: Distinct non-four-school literalist legal tradition; later Ibn Ḥazm is a major representative. Their opinions must be evidenced independently.

authorities.name: al-Ṭabarī / Jarīrī school
authorities.description: A non-four-school juristic line associated with Muḥammad b. Jarīr al-Ṭabarī. His tafsīr authorship alone is not a fiqh school relation.

authorities.name: Ibn Shubruma
authorities.description: Independent early Kufan judge and jurist. Do not infer a formally constituted madhhab from individual legal opinions.

authorities.name: ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ
authorities.description: Early Meccan legal authority. Presence in the map represents an individual teaching/reasoning tradition, not a later four-school assignment.

authorities.name: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī
authorities.description: Early Kufan jurist and one of the authorities in the pre-doctrinal school milieu.

authorities.name: al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī
authorities.description: Basran scholar with legal opinions; avoid equating the whole Basran scholarly milieu with a fixed personal school.

authorities.name: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab
authorities.description: Early Medinan juristic authority; later madhhab labels should not be retrojected into his lifetime.

authorities.name: Abū Ḥanīfa
authorities.description: Early personal-circle jurist; the later Ḥanafī doctrinal school formed over time and should not be projected backwards as a finished institution.

authorities.name: Mālik b. Anas
authorities.description: Founding eponym; distinguish his own circle and teaching from later institutional Mālikism.

authorities.name: al-Shāfiʿī
authorities.description: Founding eponym; later Shāfiʿī school organization and doctrinal convergence were subsequent processes.

authorities.name: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
authorities.description: Founding eponym; subsequent Ḥanbalī doctrinal and institutional formation is not identical to Aḥmad's lifetime.
